protocol.name: zelto_backdrop_v1

description.summary: blurred backdrop material behind a surface

protocol.description:
A client cannot read the pixels behind its own surface, so it cannot implement the blurred "material" that a phone's system surfaces (the notification shade, the dock, the on-screen keyboard, a modal sheet) are made of: a translucent panel through which the content underneath shows softly out of focus.
This protocol asks the compositor to do it. A client attaches a backdrop to one of its surfaces and declares a RECTANGLE, in surface-local coordinates, over which it wants the scene BELOW that surface blurred. The compositor composites the blurred content directly beneath the surface, masked to the rectangle (with an optional rounded/squircle corner), and the client then paints its own translucent tint, hairline and content over it as usual.
The blur radius and corner geometry are the compositor's, so every material in the system matches. The client contributes only the region and the tint.
Only the declared rectangle is blurred: a surface that is visually full-screen but whose material occupies only part of it (an idle shade that is transparent except for its panel) blurs only its panel.

interface.name: zelto_backdrop_manager_v1
interface.description: A global whose only job is to hand out a backdrop object per surface.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the manager does not affect backdrops already created.

request.name: get_backdrop

description.summary: attach a backdrop to a surface

request.description:
Create a backdrop for `surface`. The backdrop is inert until the client declares a region with set_region.
The compositor may refuse to blur behind surfaces whose stacking it does not control; in that case the backdrop simply never appears. Creating a second backdrop for the same surface replaces the first.

interface.name: zelto_backdrop_v1

description.summary: a blurred region beneath one surface

interface.description: The blurred material behind a rectangle of one surface.

request.name: set_region
request.description:
Blur the scene below this surface within the given surface-local rectangle, masking the result to a rounded rectangle of `corner_radius` (0 = square corners; the compositor uses the system's continuous-corner geometry).
A width or height of zero or less removes the backdrop, which is how a surface whose material is only sometimes present (a shade that is closed, a keyboard that is hidden) turns it off without destroying the object.
The region takes effect on the surface's next commit and persists until changed, so a client that animates its panel (a shade being dragged down) re-declares the region as the panel moves.
